paragraphs: Gilead Sciences, Inc. (including its consolidated subsidiaries, referred to as "Gilead," the "company," "we," "our" or "us") is a biopharmaceutical company that has pursued and achieved breakthroughs in medicine for more than three decades, with the goal of creating a healthier world for all people. We are committed to advancing innovative medicines to prevent and treat life-threatening diseases, including HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer. We operate in more than 35 countries worldwide, with headquarters in Foster City, California.

We have transformed care for people around the world by discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines to address unmet medical needs in virology, oncology and other therapeutic areas. Our innovative medicines represent advancements by offering first-in-class therapies, greater efficacy, enhanced modes of delivery, more convenient treatment and prevention regimens, improved resistance profiles and reduced side effects.
In 2025, our commercial portfolio included more than 25 therapies, including the following products and collaboration products with approved indications in the U.S.:

•Biktarvy® is an oral formulation dosed once a day for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in certain patients. Biktarvy is a single-tablet regimen of a fixed-dose combination of our antiretroviral medications, bictegravir, emtricitabine ("FTC") and tenofovir alafenamide ("TAF").

•Descovy® is an oral formulation indicated in combination with other antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in certain patients. Descovy is a fixed-dose combination of our antiretroviral medications, FTC and TAF. Descovy is also approved by U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") for a pre-exposure prophylaxis ("PrEP") indication to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 infection in certain at-risk patients.

•Genvoya® is an oral formulation dosed once a day for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in certain patients. Genvoya is a single-tablet regimen of a fixed-dose combination of our antiretroviral medications, elvitegravir, cobicistat, FTC and TAF.

•Odefsey® is an oral formulation dosed once a day for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in certain patients. Odefsey is a single-tablet regimen of a fixed-dose combination of our antiretroviral medications, FTC and TAF, and rilpivirine marketed by Janssen Products, LP of Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine ("Janssen").

•Sunlenca® is an HIV-1 capsid inhibitor in tablet form for oral use and as an injection for subcutaneous use. Sunlenca, in combination with other antiretroviral(s), is indicated as a twice-yearly treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance or safety considerations.

•Symtuza® is an oral formulation dosed once a day for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in certain patients. Symtuza is a single-tablet regimen of a fixed-dose combination of our antiretroviral medications, cobicistat, FTC and TAF, and Janssen's darunavir. Symtuza is commercialized by Janssen, and we receive a share in revenue for the components that we contribute. See Note 7. Collaborations and Other Arrangements of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

•Yeztugo® is an HIV-1 capsid inhibitor in tablet form for oral use and as an injection for subcutaneous use. Yeztugo is indicated for PrEP to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in certain adults and adolescents who are at risk for HIV-1 acquisition.

•Epclusa® is an oral formulation of a once-daily single-tablet regimen of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus ("HCV") infection in adults and pediatric patients 3 years of age and older with genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6: (i) without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis or (ii) with decompensated cirrhosis for use in combination with ribavirin. In addition, we have an authorized generic version of Epclusa distributed by our separate subsidiary, Asegua Therapeutics LLC.

•Livdelzi® (seladelpar) is an oral formulation of a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta agonist indicated for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis ("PBC") in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid ("UDCA") in adults who have an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA.(1)

•Vemlidy® is an oral formulation of TAF dosed once a day for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus ("HBV") infection in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with compensated liver disease.

•Tecartus® (brexucabtagene autoleucel), a suspension for intravenous infusion, is a chimeric antigen receptor ("CAR") T-cell therapy for the treatment of adult patients with (i) relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma ("MCL")(1) and (ii) relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia ("ALL").

headings: Certain of our products subject us to additional or heightened risks.
Our success depends on developing and commercializing new products or expanding the indications for existing products.
We face challenges in accurately forecasting sales because of the difficulties in predicting demand for our products and fluctuations in purchasing patterns or wholesaler inventories.
We face significant competition from global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, specialized pharmaceutical firms and generic drug manufacturers.
Our existing products are subject to pricing and reimbursement pressures from government agencies and other third parties, including required discounts and rebates.
We may experience adverse impacts resulting from the importation of our products from lower price markets or the distribution of illegally diverted or counterfeit versions of our products.
Product Development and Supply Chain Risks
We face risks in our clinical trials, including the potential for unfavorable results, delays in anticipated timelines and disruption.
We are impacted by evolving laws, regulations and legislative or regulatory actions applicable to the healthcare industry.
We face potentially significant liability and increased expenses from litigation and government investigations relating to our products and operations.
Our business has been, and may in the future be, adversely affected by outbreaks of epidemic, pandemic or contagious diseases.
We face risks associated with our global operations.
paragraphs: In evaluating our business, you should carefully consider the following discussion of material risks, events and uncertainties that make an investment in us speculative or risky in addition to the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. A manifestation of any of the following risks and uncertainties could, in circumstances we may or may not be able to accurately predict, materially and adversely affect our business and operations, growth, reputation (including the commercial or scientific reputation of our products), prospects, product pipeline and sales, operating and financial results, financial condition, cash flows, liquidity and stock price. We note these factors for investors as permitted by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. It is not possible to predict or identify all such factors; our operations could also be affected by factors, events or uncertainties that are not presently known to us or that we currently do not consider to present significant risks to our operations. Therefore, you should not consider the following risks to be a complete statement of all the potential risks or uncertainties that we face. Moreover, some of the factors, events and contingencies discussed below may have occurred in the past, but the disclosures below are not representations as to whether or not the factors, events or contingencies have occurred in the past, and instead reflect our beliefs and opinions as to the factors, events or contingencies that could materially and adversely affect us in the future.

We receive a substantial portion of our revenue from sales of our products for the treatment and prevention of HIV infection. We may be unable to sustain or increase sales of our HIV products for any number of reasons, including market share gains by competitive products, including generics, or the inability to introduce new HIV medications necessary to remain competitive. In such case, we may need to scale back our operations, including our future drug development and spending on research and development ("R&D") efforts.
Advancing a novel and personalized therapy, such as Yescarta or Tecartus, which are chimeric antigen receptor ("CAR") T-cell therapies, creates significant challenges, including:
•developing and maintaining a robust and reliable process for engineering a patient's T cells in our facilities and infusing them back into the patient;
•conditioning patients with chemotherapy in advance of administering our therapy, which may increase the risk of adverse side effects; and

•securing sufficient supply of other medications to manage side effects, such as tocilizumab and corticosteroids, which may not be available in sufficient quantities, may not adequately control the side effects and/or may have detrimental impacts on the efficacy of cell therapy.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis is intended to provide material information around events and uncertainties known to management that are relevant to an assessment of the financial condition and results of operations of Gilead and should therefore be read in conjunction with our audited Consolidated Financial Statements and the related notes thereto and other disclosures included as part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K (including the disclosures under Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors). Additional information related to the comparison of our results of operations and liquidity and capital resources between the years 2024 and 2023 is included in Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of our 2024 Form 10-K filed with U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Gilead Sciences, Inc. (including its consolidated subsidiaries, referred to as "Gilead," the "company," "we," "our" or "us") is a biopharmaceutical company that has pursued and achieved breakthroughs in medicine for more than three decades, with the goal of creating a healthier world for all people. We are committed to advancing innovative medicines to prevent and treat life-threatening diseases, including HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer. We operate in more than 35 countries worldwide, with headquarters in Foster City, California.

Our strategic ambitions are to (i) bring 10+ transformative therapies to patients by 2030 (tracking since 2020); (ii) be a biotech employer and partner of choice; and (iii) deliver shareholder value in a sustainable and responsible manner. Our strategic priorities, as refreshed in late 2025, to deliver on these ambitions include: (i) maximize impact of long-acting HIV therapies; (ii) accelerate our pipeline build in oncology and inflammation; (iii) adopt and scale artificial intelligence to transform how we work; (iv) prioritize investments for highest impact; and (v) strengthen collaboration to accelerate innovation.

During 2025, we delivered growth in our HIV product sales, introduced Yeztugo, the first and only twice-yearly HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis ("PrEP") option available in the U.S., and expanded Livdelzi's market share in the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis ("PBC"). As evidenced by various late-stage clinical trial updates in HIV and oncology, we continued to invest in our business and research and development ("R&D") pipeline through advancement of our portfolio and broadening of available therapies, including through acquisitions and collaborations. Meanwhile, we maintained our financial position by lowering operating expenses, repaying senior notes coming due and providing shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases. The following represents a summary of notable business updates and events since the filing of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, including certain items from our press releases, which readers are encouraged to review in full as available on our website at www.gilead.com. The content on the referenced website does not constitute a part of and is not incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

•Announced positive topline Phase 3 results from the ARTISTRY-1 and ARTISTRY-2 trial, evaluating our investigational daily oral single-tablet regimen of bictegravir 75mg and lenacapavir 50mg ("BIC/LEN") for virologically suppressed adults with HIV. BIC/LEN met its primary endpoint, demonstrating non-inferiority to baseline multi-tablet antiviral regimens (ARTISTRY-1) and Biktarvy (ARTISTRY-2).

•Announced settlement agreements to resolve Biktarvy patent litigation with generic manufacturers Lupin Ltd., Cipla Ltd. and Laurus Labs Ltd. Under the agreements, the earliest date the three generic manufacturers can market a generic version of full dose Biktarvy in the U.S. is April 1, 2036, subject to standard acceleration provisions. This is more than two years later than our previous loss of exclusivity projection for Biktarvy (December 2033).
•Received a strong recommendation for the use of twice-yearly injectable Yeztugo (lenacapavir) for HIV PrEP in the new U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidelines.

•Announced a partnership with the U.S. State Department and the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief ("PEPFAR") to deliver lenacapavir for HIV PrEP for up to two million people over three years in countries supported by both PEPFAR and the Global Fund.

•Received European Commission ("EC") marketing authorization for Yeytuo (lenacapavir) for PrEP to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in adults and adolescents with increased HIV-1 acquisition risk.
•Received U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approval for Yeztugo (lenacapavir) for PrEP to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35kg.

•Announced that FDA had placed a clinical hold on the HIV treatment trials of GS-1720 and/or GS-4182, including the WONDERS-1 and WONDERS-2 trials. These drug candidates are investigational and not approved anywhere globally.

•Announced that we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all of the outstanding common stock of Arcellx, Inc. ("Arcellx"), providing us with full control of its leading pipeline candidate, anitocabtagene autoleucel, an investigational BCMA-directed CAR-T cell therapy for patients with relapsed and/or refractory multiple myeloma. This transaction is anticipated to close during the second quarter of 2026, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions.

•Announced the discontinuation of the Phase 3 STAR-221 study, in partnership with Arcus Biosciences, Inc. ("Arcus"), evaluating the anti-TIGIT antibody domvanalimab ("dom") plus zimberelimab ("zim") and chemotherapy in first-line HER2- advanced gastric and esophageal cancers. The decision was based on the recommendation of the Independent Data Monitoring Committee, following review of data from a pre-specified interim analysis. Additionally, Gilead and Arcus will discontinue the Phase 2 EDGE-Gastric study evaluating dom and zim regimens in upper gastrointestinal cancers. Dom and zim are investigational products and are not approved anywhere globally.

•Announced that our Phase 3 ASCENT-07 study of Trodelvy evaluating sacituzumab govitecan-hziy ("SG") as a first-line treatment post-endocrine therapy in hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative ("HR+/HER2-") metastatic breast cancer patients did not meet the primary endpoint of progression-free survival. Overall survival is a key secondary endpoint and was not mature at the time of the primary analysis; however, an early trend was observed favoring patients treated with Trodelvy compared to chemotherapy.

paragraphs: Gilead Sciences, Inc. (包含其合併子公司，簡稱為 "Gilead," "公司," "我們," "我們的" 或 "我們") 是一家生物科技公司，自三十多年前以來，持續追求並實現醫藥領域的突破，目標是為所有人創造更健康的未來。我們致力於發展創新藥物，以預防和治療危及生命的疾病，包括艾滋病、病毒性肝炎、COVID-19 和癌症。我們在全球超過 35 個國家運營，總部設於美國加州福斯特城。
我們透過發現、開發並提供創新藥物，改變了全球人們的醫療照護方式，以解決病毒學、腫瘤學及其他治療領域未被滿足的醫療需求。我們的創新藥物代表了進步，提供首創新療法、更高的療效、更有效的給藥方式、更方便的治療與預防方案、改善的抗藥性表現及減少的副作用。
2025 年，我們的商業產品組合包含超過 25 種治療方案，包括以下產品及與合作夥伴共同開發且在美國已核准適應症的產品：
•Biktarvy® 是一種口服製劑，每日服用一次，用於治療特定患者的 HIV-1 感染。Biktarvy 是一種單一藥片組合劑型，包含我們的抗逆轉錄病毒藥物，bictegravir、emtricitabine ("FTC") 和 tenofovir alafenamide ("TAF")。
•Descovy® 是一種口服製劑，與其他抗逆轉錄病毒藥物組合使用，用於治療特定患者的 HIV-1 感染。Descovy 是一種固定劑量組合劑型，包含我們的抗逆轉錄病毒藥物，FTC 和 TAF。Descovy 也已獲得美國食品藥物管理局 ("FDA") 批准，作為預防性藥物 ("PrEP") 用於降低特定高風險患者透過性行為感染 HIV-1 的風險。
•Genvoya® 是一種口服製劑，每日服用一次，用於治療特定患者的 HIV-1 感染。Genvoya 是一種單一藥片組合劑型，包含我們的抗逆轉錄病毒藥物，elvitegravir、cobicistat、FTC 和 TAF。
•Odefsey® 是一種口服製劑，每日服用一次，用於治療特定患者的 HIV-1 感染。Odefsey 是一種單一藥片組合劑型，包含我們的抗逆轉錄病毒藥物，FTC 和 TAF，以及由 Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine ("Janssen") 的 Janssen Products, LP 市場推廣的 rilpivirine。
•Sunlenca® 是一種 HIV-1 質體抑制劑，以口服藥片形式及皮下注射形式使用。Sunlenca 與其他抗逆轉錄病毒藥物組合使用，用於治療 HIV-1 感染的重度治療經驗成人患者，這些患者因抗藥性、不耐受性或安全性考量而無法繼續現有抗逆轉錄病毒治療方案，且感染多重藥物抗性 HIV-1。

•Symtuza® 是一種口服製劑，每日一次用於治療 HIV-1 感染的特定患者。Symtuza 是本公司抗逆轉錄病毒藥物 cobicistat、FTC 和 TAF，以及 Janssen 的 darunavir 組合的固定劑量單一錠劑。Symtuza 由 Janssen 銷售，本公司就本公司所貢獻的零組件取得收入。請參閱本年度報告 10-K 表單 Part II, Item 8 所包含的財務會計彙編附註第 7 節：合作及其他安排。
•Yeztugo® 是一種 HIV-1 膜囊抑制劑，為口服錠劑及皮下注射用液體。Yeztugo 用於 PrEP（預防性暴露前）以降低特定成人及青少年因性行為而感染 HIV-1 的風險。

•Epclusa® 是一種口服製劑，為每日一次的單一錠劑，包含 sofosbuvir 和 velpatasvir，用於治療慢性丙型肝炎病毒（"HCV"）感染的成人及 3 歲以上兒童，其基因型為 1、2、3、4、5 或 6：(i) 沒有肝硬化或有代償性肝硬化，或 (ii) 有失代償性肝硬化，並與 ribavirin 組合使用。此外，本公司有經核准的 Epclusa 仿製藥，由本公司獨立子公司 Asegua Therapeutics LLC 分銷。
•Livdelzi® (seladelpar) 是一種口服製劑，為過氧化物酶體增生性脂肪酸水解酶 δ 激動劑，用於治療原發性膽汁性肝硬化（"PBC"），與 Ursodeoxycholic Acid（"UDCA"）合併使用於對 UDCA 治療反應不足的成人，或作為單一療法用於無法耐受 UDCA 的患者。(1)
•Vemlidy® 是一種口服製劑，每日一次用於治療慢性乙型肝炎病毒（"HBV"）感染的成人及 12 歲以上兒童，其肝臟疾病為代償性。
•Tecartus® (brexucabtagene autoleucel)，為靜脈注射用懸浮液，是一種嵌合抗原受體（"CAR"）T 細胞療法，用於治療成人患者之 (i) 反覆發作或難治性 Mantle Cell Lymphoma（"MCL"）(1) 和 (ii) 反覆發作或難治性 B 細胞前驅急性淋巴細胞白血病（"ALL"）。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析旨在提供有關管理層所知之事件與不確定性的重要資訊，這些資訊與評估 Gilead 財務狀況及營運結果相關，因此應與我們經審計之合併財務報表及其相關附註，以及本年度報表 10-K 所包含之其他揭露資訊一併閱讀（包括 Part I, Item 1A. 風險因素部分之揭露）。有關 2024 年與 2023 年營運結果及流動性與資本資源比較之額外資訊，請參閱我們 2024 年報表 10-K 中 Item 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析，該報表已向美國證券交易委員會提交。
Gilead Sciences, Inc.（包括其合併子公司，簡稱為 "Gilead"、"公司"、"我們"、"我們的" 或 "我們"）為一生物科技公司，自三十多年前以來，持續追求並實現醫藥領域的突破，目標為創造一個更健康的社會。我們致力於發展創新藥物，以預防及治療危及生命的疾病，包括艾滋病、病毒性肝炎、COVID-19 及癌症。我們在全球超過 35 個國家營運，總部設於美國加州福斯特城。

我們的戰略目標為 (i) 到 2030 年為患者提供 10 項以上具變革性的治療方案（自 2020 年開始追蹤）；(ii) 成為生物科技領域的僱主與合作夥伴首選；(iii) 以可持續且負責任的方式為股東創造價值。我們的戰略優先事項，於 2025 年末重新審視後，以實現這些目標，包括：(i) 最大化長效型艾滋病治療方案的影響力；(ii) 加速在腫瘤學與發炎領域的產品線建設；(iii) 採用並擴展人工智慧，以改變我們的工作方式；(iv) 優先投資於最高影響力的領域；(v) 加強合作，加速創新。

2025 年，我們在艾滋病產品銷售上實現成長，推出 Yeztugo，這是美國首個且唯一可每兩年服用一次的艾滋病預防藥物（"PrEP"），並擴大 Livdelzi 在治療原發性膽汁性肝硬化（"PBC"）的市場佔有率。根據艾滋病與腫瘤學領域多項晚期臨牀試驗的更新資訊，我們持續投資於業務與研究與開發（"R&D"）產品線，透過產品組合的進步與可用治療方案的擴張，包括透過收購與合作。同時，我們維持財務狀況，透過降低營運費用、償還到期的優先債券，以及透過股息與股票回購提供股東回報。以下為自我們提交 2024 年度報表 10-K 以來的重要業務更新與事件摘要，包括部分來自我們新聞稿的資訊，讀者被鼓勵完整閱讀我們網站上所提供的資訊，網址為 www.gilead.com。參考網站上的資訊不構成本年度報表 10-K 的一部分，亦未被引用納入本年度報表 10-K。
• 公告 ARTISTRY-1 與 ARTISTRY-2 試驗的正面初步結果，評估我們正在研發的每日口服單一藥片組合（bictegravir 75mg 與 lenacapavir 50mg（"BIC/LEN"））對已達病毒學控制的成人艾滋病患者的療效。BIC/LEN 達到其主要終點，顯示與基線多藥片抗病毒療法（ARTISTRY-1）及 Biktarvy（ARTISTRY-2）相比，具有非劣效性。
• 公告與仿製藥廠 Lupin Ltd.、Cipla Ltd. 與 Laurus Labs Ltd. 解決 Biktarvy 專利訴訟的協議。根據協議，這三家仿製藥廠可在美國市場銷售完整劑量 Biktarvy 的仿製藥最早為 2036 年 4 月 1 日，視標準加速條款而定。這比我們原先預期的 Biktarvy 獨佔權喪失時間（2033 年 12 月）晚了兩年以上。
• 收到美國疾病控制與預防中心（CDC）最新指南中對每兩年注射一次的 Yeztugo（lenacapavir）用於艾滋病預防（PrEP）的強烈建議。
• 公告與美國國務院及美國總統艾滋病應急計畫（"PEPFAR"）合作，為受 PEPFAR 與全球基金支持的國家內最多兩百萬人提供 lenacapavir 用於艾滋病預防（PrEP），持續三年。
•取得歐洲委員會（"EC"）核准，核准Yeytuo（lenacapavir）用於PrEP，以降低成人及青少年因性行為而感染HIV-1的風險，且這些人具有較高的HIV-1感染風險。
•取得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，核准Yeztugo（lenacapavir）用於PrEP，以降低成人及青少年體重至少35公斤者因性行為而感染HIV的風險。
•宣佈FDA對GS-1720及/或GS-4182的HIV治療試驗發出臨牀暫停令，包括WONDERS-1及WONDERS-2試驗。這些藥物候選品為研究中藥物，目前全球未核准。
•宣佈本公司與Arcellx, Inc.（"Arcellx"）簽訂最終協議，取得其所有發行普通股，使本公司取得其領先候選品anitocabtagene autoleucel的完全控制權，此候選品為一種針對BCMA的CAR-T細胞治療，用於治療復發及/或難治性多發性骨髓瘤患者。此交易預計於2026年第二季完成，視是否符合或豁免慣例關閉條件而定。

•宣佈停止Phase 3 STAR-221試驗，與Arcus Biosciences, Inc.（"Arcus"）合作進行，評估anti-TIGIT單株抗體domvanalimab（"dom"）加上zimberelimab（"zim"）及化療在第一線HER2-晚期胃癌及食道癌的應用。此決定基於獨立資料監測委員會根據預設中期分析資料的建議。此外，Gilead與Arcus將停止Phase 2 EDGE-Gastric試驗，評估dom與zim方案在上消化道癌症的應用。dom與zim為研究中產品，目前全球未核准。
•宣佈本公司Phase 3 ASCENT-07試驗評估Trodelvy用於荷爾蒙受體陽性、人類表皮生長因子受體2陰性（"HR+/HER2-")轉移性乳癌患者，在接受荷爾蒙治療後作為第一線治療，未達成主要終點進展無效生存期。總體生存期為關鍵次要終點，但在主要分析時尚未成熟；然而，在分析時觀察到治療組患者較化療組有較佳的早期趨勢。

headings: 我們部分產品使我們面臨額外或更高的風險。
我們的成功取決於開發並商業化新產品或擴展現有產品的適應症。
我們在準確預測銷售額方面面臨挑戰，這是因為預測產品需求的困難以及採購模式或經銷商存貨的波動。
我們面臨來自全球製藥與生物科技公司、專業製藥公司及仿製藥製造商的重大競爭。
我們現有產品面臨來自政府機構及其他第三方的價格與給付壓力，包括必須提供的折扣與回扣。
我們可能因產品從低價市場進口或非法轉運或假冒版本的產品分銷而遭受不利影響。
產品開發與供應鏈風險
我們在臨牀試驗中面臨風險，包括可能產生不利結果、預期時間表的延誤以及中斷。
我們受制於醫療保健產業適用的法規、法律及立法或法規行動的變化。
我們可能因產品及營運相關的訴訟及政府調查而面臨潛在重大賠償責任及增加的費用。
我們的業務已受到，且未來可能繼續受到疫情、大流行或傳染性疾病爆發的影響。
我們在全球營運中面臨相關風險。
paragraphs: 在評估我們的業務時，您應謹慎考慮下列有關重大風險、事件及不確定性之討論，這些因素使投資我們的行為具有投機性或風險，除了本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊外。任何下列風險與不確定性之表現，可能在我們可能或無法準確預測的情況下，對我們的業務與運作、成長、聲譽（包括我們產品之商業或科學聲譽）、前景、產品開發路線圖與銷售、營運與財務結果、財務狀況、現金流、流動性及股票價格造成重大且不利的影響。我們根據1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案之規定，向投資者說明這些因素。無法預測或識別所有這些因素；我們的運作也可能受到目前未知或我們目前認為對運作不具重大風險之因素、事件或不確定性之影響。因此，您不應將下列風險視為我們所面臨所有潛在風險或不確定性之完整陳述。此外，部分下列討論之因素、事件及待處理事項可能已發生於過去，但下列揭露並非表示這些因素、事件或待處理事項是否已發生於過去，而是反映我們對可能對我們未來造成重大且不利影響之因素、事件或待處理事項之信念與意見。
我們從治療與預防HIV感染之產品銷售中獲取相當大比例之營業收入。我們可能無法維持或增加HIV產品之銷售，原因可能包括競爭產品（包括仿製藥）之市佔率提升，或無法推出必要之新HIV藥物以保持競爭力。在這種情況下，我們可能需要縮減運作，包括未來之藥物開發與研究與發展（"R&D"）經費支出。
推進一種創新且個人化之療法，例如Yescarta或Tecartus，這些為嵌合抗原受體（"CAR"）T細胞療法，會產生重大挑戰，包括：
•在本公司設施中開發並維持一個強而有力且可靠之流程，用以工程化患者的T細胞並將其重新輸回患者體內；
•在施予我們療法前，對患者進行化療以準備，這可能會增加不良副作用之風險；以及
•確保足夠之其他藥物供應以管理副作用，例如tocilizumab與類固醇，這些藥物可能無法以足夠數量取得，可能無法有效控制副作用，或可能對細胞療法之療效產生負面影響。
